verses.english: Linked Discourses 10.3
1. With Indaka
With Spiky

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā gayāyaṁ viharati ṭaṅkitamañce sūcilomassa yakkhassa bhavane.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Gayā on the cut-stone ledge in the haunt of Spiky the native spirit.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena kharo ca yakkho sūcilomo ca yakkho bhagavato avidūre atikkamanti.
verses.english: Now at that time the native spirits Shaggy and Spiky were passing by not far from the Buddha.

verses.pali: Atha kho kharo yakkho sūcilomaṁ yakkhaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: So Shaggy said to Spiky,
“That’s an ascetic.”
“That’s no ascetic, he’s a faker!

verses.pali: Yāva jānāmi yadi vā so samaṇo yadi vā pana so samaṇako”ti.
verses.english: I’ll soon find out whether he’s an ascetic or a faker.”

verses.pali: Atha kho sūcilomo yakkho yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato kāyaṁ upanāmesi.
verses.english: Then Spiky went up to the Buddha and leaned up against his body,
but the Buddha pulled away.

verses.pali: Atha kho sūcilomo yakkho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Spiky said to the Buddha,
“Are you afraid, ascetic?”
“No, respectable sir, I’m not afraid.
But your touch is nasty.”
“I will ask you a question, ascetic.

verses.pali: Sace me na byākarissasi, cittaṁ vā te khipissāmi, hadayaṁ vā te phālessāmi, pādesu vā gahetvā pāragaṅgāya khipissāmī”ti.
verses.english: If you don’t answer me, I’ll drive you insane, or explode your heart, or grab you by the feet and throw you to the far shore of the Ganges!”

verses.pali: “Na khvāhaṁ taṁ, āvuso, passāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya, yo me cittaṁ vā khipeyya hadayaṁ vā phāleyya pādesu vā gahetvā pāragaṅgāya khipeyya;
verses.english: “I don’t see anyone in this world with its gods, Māras, and Divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans who could do that to me.

verses.pali: api ca tvaṁ, āvuso, puccha yadā kaṅkhasī”ti. (…)
verses.english: But anyway, ask what you wish.”
“Where do greed and hate come from?
From where spring discontent, desire, and terror?
Where do the mind’s thoughts originate,
like a crow let loose by boys.”
“Greed and hate come from here;
from here spring discontent, desire, and terror;
here’s where the mind’s thoughts originate,
like a crow let loose by boys.
Born of affection, originating in oneself,
like prop roots sprouting from a banyan;
the many kinds of attachment to sensual pleasures
are like camel’s foot creeper <j>creeping through the woods.
Those who understand where they come from
get rid of them—listen up, spirit!
They cross this flood so hard to cross,
not crossed before, so as to not be reborn.”
